dataset: Twin accuracy against days of local history
protocol: Each plant held out entirely. At k=0 every model is built from the other plants only. At k>0 the model sees the held-out plant's first k days. The scoring window is the plant's final 365 days and is identical for every k, so the curve isolates what local data buys.
finding: At daily-energy resolution a full year of the plant's own history buys about 1% error reduction: 16.70% nMAE on day one against 16.46% after 365 local days. Local machine learning is far WORSE than transfer until it has seen a full seasonal cycle: 33.8% at 30 days, 22.0% at 60, 19.9% at 90, converging to transfer only at 365. A model trained on a customer's first month is actively harmful.
why: The irradiance-to-power relationship is close to universal, so at daily aggregation there is little site-specific signal left to learn. What varies between plants is mostly a scale factor, and that comes from the nameplate rather than from history.
caveats: Daily-energy resolution only. The 15-minute twin reaches 6.61% nMAE of AC nameplate, a different metric on a different normaliser, and is not comparable to these numbers.

The scoring window here is each plant's final 365 days, which is a harder and different window from the walk-forward and leave-one-plant-out runs. Compare rows within this table, not across artifacts.
Says nothing about faults or soiling, where local reference data is known to matter a great deal.
headline: day one 16.70% nMAE, 16.46% after a year of local data: local history buys ~1% at daily resolution, and local-only ML is worse than transfer below 365 days
